rules.notes: safe_harbor=true: policy explicitly states 'Any activities conducted in a manner consistent with this policy will be considered authorized conduct and we will not initiate legal action against you.' Full safe harbor including third-party action coverage. | mass_scanning_allowed=false: set to safe default; policy says 'make a good faith effort to avoid... interruption or degradation of our service' but no explicit mass-scanning clause; safe default applied. | automated_tools_allowed=false: set to safe default; no explicit policy statement permitting automated scanning; safe default applied. | bucket_listing_allowed=true / bucket_download_allowed=false: no explicit bucket policy present; defaults applied per schema spec. | cve_age_min_days=30: no explicit CVE age requirement stated; safe default applied. | requires_ownership_proof=true: for Software Supply Chain / dependency confusion, policy explicitly requires 'verifiable proof that the dependency has been downloaded by Elastic employees or Elastic owned infrastructure'; applies to supply-chain category. For other assets default applies. | LEAKED CREDS GOTCHA: 'elastic.co credentials' is an EXPLICIT in-scope asset with severity_cap=low and bounty_eligible=true. Policy also states that for Software Supply Chain, 'actual credential exfiltration or leaks (not theoretical) from build services' is in scope at up to critical. Passive GH-leak findings for elastic.co creds therefore qualify but will be graded LOW unless chained to supply chain / build service compromise. | THIRD-PARTY TOKENS: 'Security issues in third party systems, domains, services and components fall outside this policy and are not eligible for a bounty.' Tokens found in elastic repos that belong to third parties (e.g. vendor API keys) are OOS; only tokens belonging to Elastic itself are in scope. | ACQUISITION WINDOW: Recent acquisitions are OOS for 6 months post-close. keephq.dev is explicitly marked ineligible (decommissioning). jina.ai and es.io also currently OOS per CSV. | CLOUD TESTING: Must use @wearehackerone.com email; bounty withheld if non-H1 email used. | XSS: Requires CSP bypass to be in scope; otherwise case-by-case at low.

raw_policy_excerpt:
The Elastic team appreciates the security community and shares the goal of keeping our businesses, customers, and the internet safe. Elastic values your efforts and promises to remain responsive; update you as your reports are triaged and remediated. We award bounty eligible reports at triage and hope to work together on an ongoing basis.

Elastic's bounty structure falls under two umbrellas: Product Vulnerabilities & Other. While we accept vulnerabilities on any assets that we own/control, we are _particularly_ interested in vulnerabilities in our products, and as such will pay significantly more as indicated in our bounty structure.

## What we're interested in
* Attacks that lead to compromise of Elastic user data
* Widespread compromise of Elastic user accounts
* Remote code execution on systems and applications
* Access to administrator/superuser accounts
* Arbitrary access to a user's sensitive data/functionality
* Kibana XSS and CSRF
* Access to underlying containers
* Access to unauthorized data as authenticated user
* Privilege escalation as authenticated user to non superuser
* Authenticated SSRF

##Out of scope
* Security issues in third party systems, domains, services and components fall outside this policy and are not eligible for a bounty. We encourage you to submit these to the third party owner.
* Findings that require administrative or root operating system privileges are out of scope.
* Findings in legacy or end-of-life product versions.
* Subdomain takeovers on typosquatted domains or parked/reserved domains for phishing
* Application-level Denial of Service attacks against Swiftype
* Cross-site scripting vulnerabilities that are not accompanied by a bypass of our content security policy.
* Volumetric attacks (e.g., network flooding, request flooding, port flooding, required traffic volume scaling with deployment size) are never eligible for bounty rewards.
* Recent acquisitions by Elastic are out of Scope for the Bug Bounty program for at least 6 months after the acquisition is complete.

# Software Supply Chain scope excerpt:
Actual credential exfiltration or leaks (not theoretical) from build services (below)
Dependency Confusion. When reporting dependency confusion attacks please include verifiable proof that the dependency has been downloaded by Elastic employees or Elastic owned infrastructure.

# elastic.co credentials asset:
In-scope, bounty-eligible, severity_cap=low, availability=none, confidentiality=low, integrity=none.

# Safe Harbor
Any activities conducted in a manner consistent with this policy will be considered authorized conduct and we will not initiate legal action against you. If legal action is initiated by a third party against you in connection with activities conducted under this policy, we will take steps to make it known that your actions were conducted in compliance with this policy.
